summary: The note describes the Sinai Peninsula, a peninsula in Egypt and the only part of the country located in Asia. It lies between the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the south, forming a land bridge between Asia and Africa. The note gives its area, population, and administrative division into two governorates, along with three other governorates that span the Suez Canal.
one_line: Sinai Peninsula is Egypt's only Asian territory, a land bridge between Asia and Africa lying between the Mediterranean and Red Seas.
key_facts: The Sinai Peninsula is a peninsula in Egypt and the only part of the country located in Asia.
The Sinai Peninsula is situated between the Mediterranean Sea to the north and the Red Sea to the south.
The Sinai Peninsula is a land bridge between Asia and Africa.
Sinai has a land area of about 60,000 km (23,000 sq mi).
Sinai has a population of approximately 1,400,000 people.
Administratively, the Sinai Peninsula is divided into two governorates: the South Sinai Governorate and the North Sinai Governorate.
Suez Governorate lies on the southern end of the Suez Canal and is one of three other governorates that span the Suez Canal into African Egypt.
Ismailia Governorate lies in the center of the Suez Canal and is one of three other governorates that span the Suez Canal into African Egypt.
Port Said Governorate lies in the north of the Suez Canal and is one of three other governorates that span the Suez Canal into African Egypt.
The name Sinai is given in Arabic as سيناء (Sīnāʼ), in Egyptian Arabic as سينا (Sīna), in Hebrew as סִינַי (Sinai), and in Coptic as ⲥⲓⲛⲁ.
The note gives the pronunciation of Sinai as / ˈsaɪnaɪ / (now usually).
